answer: A rolling eligibility horizon resists sybils cheaply: only identities that pass the latest challenge and hold a stake lock count, so each forged identity pays a real generation plus stake cost that grows linearly with identity count while its voting weight stays flat. That cost leg is like yarrow divination, where every stalk is spent once and extra stalks never alter a verdict. The fable is practical: ten thousand shells weigh one identity in a tally yet cost their owner ten thousand times, so mass identity inflation is self-defeating.
